news.headline: Fujifilm's 40TB LTO-10 cartridge shows up at about $494
news.summary: Chinese tech site IT Home (republished by ifeng) reported that Fujifilm's 40TB native LTO-10 cartridge was selling for $494, well under the $888.89 suggested retail price. TechRadar ran the same price story; its date could not be confirmed.
news.source: IT之家 (IT Home) via ifeng Tech
news.dateNote: ifeng timestamp 2026-09-27 07:26 Beijing time; TechRadar publication date not shown in fetched page

news.headline: Spectra Logic signs Italian distributor ICOS
news.summary: Tape library maker Spectra Logic signed a distribution deal with ICOS S.p.A., giving ICOS's Italian channel partners access to Spectra's storage products.
news.quote: Distribution agreement strengthens Spectra Logic's presence in the Italian market

news.headline: Cheap used LTO-5 drives bring tape back to homelabs
news.summary: Hackaday covered a homelab builder using a second-hand LTO-5 drive for backups, pointing out that used tapes cost about $2 per TB against roughly $16 per TB for the cheapest new hard drives.
news.quote: tape remains the god of cheap storage

news.headline: TapeArk moves old tape archives into public-cloud virtual tape libraries
news.summary: TapeArk reads customers' legacy tapes at its ingest centers and loads the data into cloud virtual tape libraries, accessed through its Nexus SaaS platform, pitching lower cost, faster access and AI analysis.
news.quote: a longitudinal dataset waiting for liberation

news.headline: LTO shipments dipped 9% in 2025, then jumped 57% in Q1 2026
news.summary: The LTO Program (HPE, IBM, Quantum) reported 160.3 EB compressed shipped in 2025, down from the 176.5 EB record in 2024, while Q1 2026 capacity shipped rose 57% year on year on LTO-9 volume and the LTO-10 ramp.
news.quote: 160.3 exabytes worth of LTO tape went out the door during 2025
news.windowNote: Outside the 2026-09-20 to 2026-10-18 window; included from the extended 2026-09-01 window. LTO.org re-posted this coverage on 2026-10-10.

ibmTotalStorage.fact: IBM TotalStorage was IBM's storage brand used on its LTO Ultrium drives (3580 stand-alone, 3588 drive models) in the early-to-mid 2000s, later replaced by System Storage and TS-series names (e.g. TS2290).
